title: Module 8 · Codes and Resuscitation
intro: Adult arrest drugs and timing, reversible causes (hyperkalemia, torsades, opioids, local anesthetic toxicity, tricyclics), bradycardia, adenosine, anaphylaxis, malignant hyperthermia and post arrest care.

cases.title: Asystole: the first drug
cases.stem: You arrive at a code. Rhythm: asystole. CPR is in progress, IV in place.

steps.q: What drug and when?

options.t: Epinephrine 1 mg IV now, then every 3 to 5 min
options.why: Non shockable rhythm: give as soon as possible (AHA).

options.t: Epinephrine 1 mg IV after the second shock
options.why: That timing is for VF/pVT; asystole is not shocked.

options.t: Atropine 1 mg IV every 3 to 5 min, max 3 mg
options.why: Removed from arrest algorithms in 2010; it is a bradycardia drug.

options.t: Vasopressin 40 units IV in place of epinephrine
options.why: Removed from the adult algorithm in 2015; no added benefit.

steps.q: What is your job during the code?

options.t: Call out epinephrine timing ("Epi due in 1 minute")
Prepare the next doses; prompt the H's and T's
Confirm weight and allergies; help record drugs and times
Run the code and assign compressor roles
options.why: The code leader runs the code.

options.t: Decide when to stop resuscitation

cases.pearl: **Asystole or PEA: epinephrine 1 mg now, every 3 to 5 minutes.**

sources.t: AHA Guidelines for CPR and Emergency Cardiovascular Care (2025)
St. Mary's code team policy, crash cart contents and post arrest order set (verify locally)

cases.title: VF: shock first
cases.stem: VF. Two shocks given, still VF.

steps.q: When does epinephrine go in for VF?

options.t: After the second shock, then every 3 to 5 min
options.why: AHA: after initial defibrillation attempts fail.

options.t: Before the first shock, then every 3 to 5 min
options.why: Shock first in VF; that early timing is for non shockable rhythms.

options.t: After the third shock, with amiodarone 300 mg
options.why: The third shock is when amiodarone or lidocaine is added.

options.t: Only after 10 minutes of CPR with no ROSC

steps.q: Still VF after the third shock. Which antiarrhythmic?

options.t: Amiodarone 300 mg IV/IO push, then 150 mg
Lidocaine 1 to 1.5 mg/kg, then 0.5 to 0.75 mg/kg
Amiodarone 150 mg over 10 minutes, then 1 mg/min
options.why: The stable VT and post ROSC dosing.

options.t: Procainamide 20 to 50 mg/min, max 17 mg/kg
options.why: For stable wide complex tachycardia, not arrest.

options.t: Adenosine 6 mg, then 12 mg

steps.q: Are calcium, bicarbonate or magnesium routine in arrest?

options.t: No; only for specific causes
options.why: Hyperkalemia, torsades, tricyclic overdose, known acidosis.

options.t: Yes, calcium chloride 1 g every code
options.why: Routine calcium is not helpful (and may harm).

options.t: Yes, bicarbonate 1 mEq/kg every 10 min
Yes, magnesium 2 g in every VF arrest

cases.pearl: **VF: shock, epi after shocks fail, amiodarone 300 then 150 (or lidocaine).**

sources.t: AHA Guidelines for CPR and Emergency Cardiovascular Care (2025)

cases.title: Hyperkalemia arrest
cases.stem: A dialysis patient who missed two sessions arrests (PEA). K was 7.8 an hour ago.

steps.q: What do you have ready?

options.t: Calcium chloride 1 g IV (or gluconate 3 g)
Regular insulin 10 units IV with dextrose 25 g
Sodium bicarbonate 50 mEq IV if acidotic
Calcium gluconate 1 g as the full arrest dose
options.why: Gluconate has a third of the calcium; 3 g matches 1 g chloride.

options.t: Sodium zirconium cyclosilicate 10 g by tube
options.why: Works over hours; not an arrest drug.

cases.pearl: **Hyperkalemia arrest: calcium, insulin + dextrose, bicarbonate if acidotic.**

sources.t: AHA Guidelines for CPR and Emergency Cardiovascular Care (2025)

cases.title: Torsades
cases.stem: Polymorphic VT with a long QT on methadone and ondansetron. Pulseless.

steps.q: Which drug besides defibrillation?

options.t: Magnesium sulfate 1 to 2 g IV push
Magnesium sulfate 4 to 6 g IV over 20 min
Procainamide 20 to 50 mg/min IV
Amiodarone 300 mg IV push alone
options.why: Prolongs QT; magnesium is the drug for torsades.

steps.q: After ROSC, what do you do with the med list?

options.t: Stop QT drugs; replace K and Mg; check CredibleMeds
options.why: Keep K above 4 and Mg above 2 commonly.

options.t: Continue methadone; stop only ondansetron
options.why: Review both; methadone dose or alternative must be addressed.

options.t: Swap ondansetron for haloperidol for nausea
Switch ondansetron to droperidol for nausea
options.why: Droperidol carries a boxed QT warning.

cases.pearl: **Torsades: magnesium 1 to 2 g. Then stop QT drugs and fix K and Mg.**

sources.t: AHA Guidelines for CPR and Emergency Cardiovascular Care (2025)

cases.title: Opioid overdose
cases.stem: An unresponsive patient on a PCA with RR 4, pinpoint pupils, pulse present.

steps.q: What do you recommend?

options.t: Bag mask breaths and naloxone 0.4 mg IV
options.why: Repeat or increase to 2 mg; 4 mg intranasal if no IV.

options.t: Naloxone 2 mg IV only, no ventilation
options.why: Ventilate first; large doses cause abrupt withdrawal.

options.t: Flumazenil 0.2 mg IV over 30 seconds
Sternal rub and a recheck in 15 minutes

steps.q: Why might naloxone wear off before the opioid?

options.t: Naloxone lasts 30 to 90 min; opioids can last longer
options.why: Repeat doses or an infusion may be needed.

options.t: Naloxone lasts 12 to 24 hours like methadone
Naloxone is cleared faster in kidney failure
Naloxone is inactivated by the PCA opioid

cases.pearl: **Opioid OD: breathe for them, naloxone 0.4 mg IV and repeat. Watch for it wearing off.**

sources.t: AHA 2023 focused update on adult ACLS (toxicology and drug use)

workup.calc: Naloxone 0.4 mg IV, repeat every 2 to 3 minutes as needed; 4 mg intranasal if no IV.

cases.title: Local anesthetic toxicity
cases.stem: Minutes after a bupivacaine nerve block, a 70 kg patient seizes and then develops wide complex bradycardia.

steps.q: What is the antidote and dose?

options.t: Lipid 20%: 1.5 mL/kg bolus, then 0.25 mL/kg/min
options.why: 105 mL over 2 to 3 minutes for 70 kg (ASRA).

options.t: Lipid 20%: 15 mL/kg bolus, then 2.5 mL/kg/min
Propofol 1 mg/kg IV for the seizure
options.why: Propofol is a lipid but too little and depresses the heart.

options.t: Naloxone 0.4 mg IV, repeated every 2 min

steps.q: How does epinephrine change in this arrest?

options.t: Smaller doses: 1 mcg/kg or less
Standard 1 mg every 3 to 5 minutes
options.why: Large epinephrine doses worsen LAST outcomes.

options.t: Double: 2 mg every 3 to 5 minutes
Replace epinephrine with vasopressin
options.why: Vasopressin is not recommended in LAST.

cases.pearl: **LAST: lipid 20% 1.5 mL/kg, then 0.25 mL/kg/min. Small epi doses.**

sources.t: Neal JM, et al. Third ASRA practice advisory on local anesthetic systemic toxicity. Reg Anesth Pain Med 2018;43:113-123

workup.calc: Lipid 20%: 1.5 mL/kg x 70 kg = **105 mL** over 2 to 3 min, then 0.25 mL/kg/min = **17.5 mL/min**.

steps.q: What do you recommend?

options.t: Sodium bicarbonate 1 to 2 mEq/kg IV, repeat
options.why: To narrow the QRS; aim pH 7.45 to 7.55.

options.t: Procainamide 20 to 50 mg/min IV
options.why: Class IA; worsens sodium channel block.

options.t: Physostigmine 1 to 2 mg IV slowly
Flumazenil 0.2 mg IV for co ingestion
options.why: Can trigger seizures in TCA overdose.

sources.t: AHA 2023 focused update on adult ACLS (toxicology and drug use)

workup.calc: Bicarbonate 1 to 2 mEq/kg (for 70 kg, 70 to 140 mEq = 1.4 to 2.8 ampules of 50 mEq), repeat to narrow QRS.

cases.title: Symptomatic bradycardia

steps.q: First drug?

options.t: Atropine 1 mg IV every 3 to 5 min, max 3 mg
Atropine 0.5 mg IV every 3 to 5 min, max 3 mg
Adenosine 6 mg rapid IV push
options.why: For SVT; slows the heart further.

options.t: Epinephrine 1 mg IV push every 3 min

steps.q: No response. Next options?

options.t: Epinephrine 2 to 10 mcg/min, dopamine, or pacing
Isoproterenol 20 mcg/min as first choice
options.why: Possible, but not the AHA first options.

options.t: Dopamine 1 to 3 mcg/kg/min "renal dose"
Atropine 1 mg more, above the 3 mg max

cases.pearl: **Brady: atropine 1 mg (max 3), then epi drip, dopamine or pacing.**

sources.t: AHA Guidelines for CPR and Emergency Cardiovascular Care (2025)

cases.title: Adenosine for SVT
cases.stem: Stable narrow complex SVT at 190. The patient has a central line.

steps.q: How is adenosine given?

options.t: Rapid IV push, then an immediate saline flush
Slow IV push over 1 to 2 minutes, no flush
options.why: It breaks down before reaching the heart.

options.t: IV piggyback over 15 minutes
Rapid push into the lower leg vein

steps.q: What dose with a central line?

options.t: 3 mg first (instead of 6 mg)
options.why: Central line or on dipyridamole; heart transplant also lower.

options.t: 12 mg first (instead of 6 mg)
options.why: 12 mg is the second peripheral dose.

options.t: 6 mg first, same as peripheral
options.why: Central lines deliver it faster and stronger.

options.t: 0.1 mg/kg first, max 6 mg

cases.pearl: **Adenosine: fast push and flush. 6 then 12; 3 mg if central line, transplant, dipyridamole.**

sources.t: AHA Guidelines for CPR and Emergency Cardiovascular Care (2025)

cases.title: Anaphylaxis
cases.setting: Infusion center · after the first dose
cases.stem: Five minutes into an IV antibiotic: hives, wheeze, BP 80/45.

steps.q: First drug and route?

options.t: Epinephrine 0.5 mg IM (1 mg/mL), outer thigh
Diphenhydramine 50 mg IV as the first drug
options.why: Antihistamines do not treat shock or airway swelling.

options.t: Epinephrine 1 mg IV push (0.1 mg/mL)
options.why: The arrest dose; dangerous with a pulse.

options.t: Epinephrine 0.5 mg SC into the upper arm
options.why: SC is slower; IM thigh is preferred.

steps.q: Not responding to IM doses. Next?

options.t: Epinephrine infusion and IV fluids
More diphenhydramine 50 mg IV
Methylprednisolone 125 mg IV alone
Famotidine 20 mg IV and observe

cases.pearl: **Anaphylaxis: epi 0.5 mg IM thigh. Never 1 mg IV push when there is a pulse.**

sources.t: AHA Guidelines for CPR and Emergency Cardiovascular Care (2025)

cases.title: Malignant hyperthermia
cases.stem: Rising end tidal CO2, rigidity and fever after succinylcholine and sevoflurane.

steps.q: What is the drug and dose?

options.t: Dantrolene 2.5 mg/kg IV, repeat until resolved
Dantrolene 1 mg/kg IV once, max 10 mg/kg
options.why: 1 mg/kg is too low a starting dose; repeat as needed.

options.t: Acetaminophen 1 g IV and cooling only
options.why: Does not stop the muscle reaction.

options.t: Bromocriptine 2.5 mg by tube

steps.q: What pharmacist detail matters most?

options.t: Where the MH cart is and which product you stock
options.why: Ryanodex reconstitutes much faster than Dantrium.

options.t: That dantrolene must be refrigerated
That dantrolene needs a 0.2 micron filter
That dantrolene is only given IM

cases.pearl: **MH: dantrolene 2.5 mg/kg, repeat. Know your cart.**

sources.t: NYSORA: updated guidelines for managing malignant hyperthermia (MHAUS based)
St. Mary's code team policy, crash cart contents and post arrest order set (verify locally)

workup.calc: Example for an 80 kg adult: dantrolene 2.5 mg/kg = **200 mg** IV, repeat until signs resolve.

cases.title: After ROSC
cases.stem: Pulse is back after VF arrest. Comatose. BP 82/48.

steps.q: Which targets are common?

options.t: SBP at least 90 and MAP at least 65
SpO2 about 92 to 98%, avoiding hyperoxia
Temperature control with fever prevention
SpO2 100% on FiO2 1.0 for 24 hours
Glucose 80 to 110 mg/dL

steps.q: Amiodarone infusion after VF. Usual regimen?

options.t: 1 mg/min for 6 h, then 0.5 mg/min for 18 h
options.why: After the 150 mg load if not already given.

options.t: 0.5 mg/min for 6 h, then 1 mg/min for 18 h
2 mg/min for 6 h, then 1 mg/min for 18 h
10 mg/min for 15 min, then 1 mg/min
options.why: Confuses the 150 mg over 10 min load rate.

cases.pearl: **Post ROSC: MAP 65+, SpO2 92 to 98, temp below 37.5, amio 1 then 0.5 mg/min.**
